articles.title: DVAC books ex-DMK minister Durai Murugan in Rs 4,730-Cr illegal sand quarry case; fifth ex-DMK minister to face probe
articles.description: In another setback to the DMK, its fifth former minister is now facing a DVAC probe. Durai Murugan, the party’s general secretary, who served as PWD Minister in the governments led by M Karunanidhi and MK Stalin, is facing an investigation into an alleged multi-crore illegal sand mining case. After the TVK government came to power in Tamil Nadu following the May Assembly elections, its anti-corruption arm has been targeting former DMK ministers over their alleged misdeeds and corruption-related matters. Following a detailed inquiry into complaints lodged by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and two others, and after finding substantial evidence establishing a prima facie case, the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) booked Durai Murugan, the then Water Resources Department (WRD) Minister, as the first accused. The case also names the then Engineers-in-Chief A Muthaiya and Ramamoorthy, 14 WRD officials, 10 private individuals and firms, and others. Big: DVAC books former minister and DMK general secretary @DuraimuruganDmk in connection with illegal sand mining that happened between 2021 and 2024. Press note by DVAC also says that contracts were given through limited tenders instead of open letters with fabricated vouchers. https://t.co/UCzwDJHjzc — Sanjeevee sadagopan (@sanjusadagopan) November 6, 2026 DVAC registers case based on ED and anti-corruption NGO complaints A government release dated November 6 stated that the DVAC headquarters had registered Case Crime No. 08/2026 against Durai Murugan and others, based on complaints received from the ED, Chennai, S Tamilselvan and Jayaram Venkatesan, convenor of Arappor Iyakkam, an anti-corruption NGO. ED மற்றும் அறப்போர் புகாரில் முன்னாள் அமைச்சர் துரைமுருகன், 17 பொது ஊழியர்கள் மற்றும் 10 தனி நபர்கள் / தனியார் நிறுவனங்கள் மீது ரூ 1427 கோடி ஆற்று மணல் கொள்ளை ஊழல் வழக்கு பதிவு! அறப்போர் தொடரும் ! pic.twitter.com/mDfqVjA0UK — Jayaram Venkatesan (@JayaramArappor) November 6, 2026 The statement claimed that alleged corruption and malpractices took place between 2021 and 2024 in matters relating to river and sand mining operations in 28 quarries at various locations across Tamil Nadu. These included awarding contracts through limited tenders instead of open tenders, carrying out sand mining beyond the approved mining plans, illegally fabricating vouchers in the name of permit slips and using them as genuine documents, and transporting sand illegally. Also Read: Tamil Nadu: Supreme Court upholds FIR order against DMK leader KN Nehru in Rs 634-crore cash-for-jobs scam These activities allegedly caused a wrongful loss of Rs.1,427,34,23,059 to the government in respect of four out of the 28 quarries. 34 locations searched; 825 documents seized As part of the probe, searches were conducted on November 6 at 34 locations in Chennai, Pudukkottai, Tiruchy, Karur, Vellore, Madurai, Dindigul, Sivaganga, Coimbatore, Salem, Namakkal and Puducherry. The DVAC seized 825 incriminating documents, 11 electronic gadgets and three bank locker keys connected to the investigation. The investigation, the government statement said, was continuing. CM Vijay is on a mission – DVAC has raided 30 places in connection with illegal sand mining! This has rarely happened under previous regimes. The concerned ministers themselves were often the ones running the racket. In 2024, the Enforcement Directorate sent a detailed dossier… pic.twitter.com/DFXGNHDB9p — Praveen (@DrPraveenwrites) November 6, 2026 ED had flagged alleged Rs.4,730-crore illegal sand mining scam The probe stems from an ED communication flagging an alleged Rs.4,730-crore illegal sand mining scam to the Tamil Nadu government during its investigation into a case under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). The ED engaged experts from IIT Kanpur and other central agencies to assess the extent of illegal sand mining. The investigation established that a huge quantity of sand had been illegally mined. The ED shared the information it had gathered with the then Director General of Police (DGP) and head of the police force in compliance with its statutory obligation under Section 66(2) of the PMLA, 2002, which mandates the ED to share such information with other law-enforcement agencies. Although the information was shared two years ago, the then DMK government did not act on it, for reasons best known to it. Supreme Court had cleared ED’s path to question district collectors Earlier, the ED submitted a report to the Madras High Court stating that it possessed credible scientific evidence based on technical studies conducted at all mining sites. These included drone and Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) surveys, bathymetric surveys and satellite imagery processing, among other methods, which established that rampant illegal sand mining had taken place within the jurisdictions of various district collectors. The ED had summoned the collectors for questioning, which they opposed by moving the courts. A Bench of Justices Bela M. Trivedi and Pankaj Mithal, in February 2024, stayed the interim order of the Madras High Court, which had previously put the ED’s summons on hold. The Supreme Court observed that state governments and their officials were bound by the PMLA, and that Section 50 of the Act empowered the ED to summon any person to provide information or evidence. The searches included the premises of two partners of a private infrastructure firm in Tiruchy, Yembal and Thiruvakudi. Former DMK functionary had alleged Rs.60,000-crore wealth In late 2023, Gudiyatham Kumaran, who was the deputy secretary of the DMK’s propaganda wing, publicly alleged that Durai Murugan and his son had amassed nearly ₹60,000 crore through large-scale illegal sand mining operations across Tamil Nadu. Durai Murugan’s political positions and family wedding draw criticism Durai Murugan, an authority on the Cauvery water dispute and other river-related issues, is a staunch Dravidian ideologue known for mocking Hindu customs and Hindu Gods. However, he performed his granddaughter’s marriage with Brahmins conducting the rituals in Sanskrit. The Dravidar Kazhagam and others strongly criticised him over this.
